summary.intent: Work through the callisto v1 hardening plan: ship planned fix PRs in parallel lanes, get recommendations for the pending owner decisions, and keep moving until the decision-free v1 work is done.
summary.outcome: Opened and merged many PRs (W2 retry fix, W1 test, W0 docs, R5 stack, R3 split, T06 colon rejection E316). Opened PRs for CI hygiene (#271), E317 bare-name rejection (#272), pre-mode no-repeat bump (E318), range hard-stop (E319), dist-tag/snapshot refusal, and a dead-bare-code deletion. The last one was being committed when the transcript ended. Decisions were accepted, including lockstep versioning with all four crates going to 1.0.

repo: Plans and tracking files live locally in .claude/plans/ (git-excluded via .git/info/exclude) and must never go in a commit or PR.
Standing rules: commits must be signed (plain git commit) and PRs must not be drafts; no session links in commits or PRs per AGENTS.md.
Each change needs a changeset (.changeset/*.md), except test-only and docs-only PRs; spec criteria in docs/specs/*.json, docs/errors.md and architecture docs are updated alongside code.
just ci is the gate; the background wrapper's exit code is not reliable, so the log's own exit= line must be read (a fmt-check failure showed exit=1 while the wrapper said 0).
callisto-model is MIT and the other crates are FSL, so it stays a separate crate. Consolidation to four published crates already shipped in #157; callisto-fixtures is dev-only.
The sandbox rejects inline env, heredocs, compound commands, and scripts mentioning git; workarounds are script files, the Write tool, or the Edit tool. Edits are limited to the current worktree.
macOS bash lacks mapfile and BSD sed rejects some one-liners, which affects generated workflow templates and local scripts.
Generated workflow templates live in crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/*.tmpl, and init.rs inline tests were moved to init/tests.rs.
Native stacks of PRs are linked with gh stack.
Michi (sibling repo) is moving to lockstep versioning with fewer crates (branch refactor/michi-core-merge).

code.finding: A package whose version is tagged at HEAD must still have all operations (registry, tag, GitHub release) observed. Treating a tag on HEAD as 'released' was the SYS-RETRY defect.
Tag inspection must read only the object type, not annotation text, so multi-paragraph or signed tag messages don't error.
The large derive function was split into stage functions after characterization snapshots; uploads_by_package moved into OpIndex. Mutation tests confirmed the snapshots catch regressions.

workflow: Write the failing black-box test first, and prove tests can fail by mutation (revert the fix or drop a persist) before trusting them.
For pure moves and refactors, commit characterization snapshots first, then do a mechanical move with snapshots unchanged.
Prove fixes with the real tool (real binary, real jq) rather than fakes; fakes hid the earlier gh bug.
Scripted bulk edits can corrupt unrelated text (double prefixes, altered comments); review the staged diff before committing.
Get an independent agent review on the riskiest PR; it surfaced real defects in #202.
Check closing state (PR draft flag, signature verification, hosted CI) before reporting a PR as ready.

friction: Earlier mistake: the plan was put in PR #201 and had to be closed and moved to a local file.
Sandbox restrictions on heredocs, inline env, compound commands and git-mentioning scripts forced many workarounds.
Background-session limits prevented editing the shared-checkout plan file from a worktree, so the status couldn't be recorded at first.
The scripted bare-to-qualified conversion double-prefixed names and altered unrelated comments, requiring fixups.
Rebase conflicts in docs/errors.md occurred repeatedly across stacked E317/E318/E319 PRs.
The wrapper reported exit 0 while CI had actually failed fmt-check.
The #204 docs refresh still lists SYS-RETRY/T08-RETRY and needs a follow-up once #202 merges.
